title: The Pipe Under the Bow
topic_used: Bearspaw South Feeder Main: 2024 and 2025 breaks, Independent Review Panel finding that the risk was identified after the 2004 McKnight failure and inspections designated 2017/2020/2022 did not occur, and the new steel pipe (microtunnelled under the Bow) being connected under Stage 4 from Nov 4, 2026
central_figure: Risks behind the June 5, 2024 failure were identified twenty years earlier, after the 2004 McKnight feeder main failure (Independent Review Panel Final Report, Jan 6, 2026, p. 17); the pipe carries up to ~60% of Calgary's potable water

title: Calgary's 2027 budget: what the preliminary numbers say
topic_used: Preliminary 2027–2030 budget figures Council released Sept 29, 2026 (C2026-0749 Rev. Att. 1): 2027 new ongoing operating requests $528M, available funding $144M, remaining $384M paired with a 15% tax revenue increase (council's July 28 guidance); City scenarios hold 4.2–5.0%/yr, improve 20.2% in 2027; +$36/month City property tax on the $706,000 median home; proposed budget out Nov 10, deliberations Nov 23
changed_from_calendar: Calendar asked for 2027 'budget adjustments … by service'. 2027 starts a new four-year cycle, and the proposed budget with service-level detail is only released Nov 10, 2026 (the day after this run); the only official figures public today (Sept 29 released deck) have no per-service breakdown, so the angle became the 2027 operating numbers, scenarios and typical-home impact.
central_figure: 2027: $528M in new ongoing operating requests, $144M available funding, remaining $384M paired with a 15% property tax revenue increase (City of Calgary C2026-0749 Rev. Att. 1, slide 28, Sept 29, 2026)

title: Who was Deerfoot? The runner behind Deerfoot Trail
topic_used: Deerfoot (Api-kai-ees), Siksika (Blackfoot) runner and nephew of head chief Crowfoot: autumn 1886 ten-mile race in Calgary, beat J. W. Stokes of Birmingham by a full lap; miscount claim, race rerun; entered after Stokes had run six laps and still passed him, finishing in 54:30; Deerfoot Trail named in his memory in the 1970s (DCB)
central_figure: In the autumn 1886 ten-mile race in Calgary, Deerfoot beat J. W. Stokes by a full lap; in the rerun he entered after Stokes had completed six laps and still passed him (Dictionary of Canadian Biography, 'Api-kai-ees')
post_note: Scheduled 20:20 with custom thumbnail; confirmed PUBLISHED on all three at 20:23, no warnings.

title: The Georgia town behind Calgary's Field of Crosses
topic_used: Field of Crosses origin: Calgary businessman Murray McCann saw roadside crosses honouring the fallen in Menlo, Georgia, took the idea to the Calgary Poppy Fund; a few hundred crosses on Memorial Drive in 2009 (VAC 500; board chair 300), more than 3,700 in 2026, honouring thousands of southern Albertans who died defending Canada
central_figure: More than 3,700 crosses in 2026 (Global News, Nov 4, 2026), from a few hundred in 2009
